verifications.claim: id: PAT_BACAR; nameMain: Bacar; nameSystem: non_hereditary_patronymic; transmissionMode: non_hereditary; designatedSocialUnit: individual

candidates.title: « NOM, Prénom » : une étape vers l'uniformisation culturelle ? Identité et statut juridique à Mayotte
candidates.quote: De ce système les Comoriens n'ont retenu que la partie centrale, constituée du nom individuel, suivi du nom du père.
candidates.supports: A comorian personal name is an individual name followed by the father's name, which supports non_hereditary_patronymic and individual unit. The article does not mention the spelling Bacar (it cites Bakari); it does not establish the link to the Comorian people. Opened and read in this session.

verifications.claim: id: PAT_BAKALA; nameMain: Bakala; nameSystem: clan_name; transmissionMode: other; designatedSocialUnit: clan

candidates.title: Les noms propres et leurs secrets dans la civilisation précoloniale des Beembe du Congo-Brazzaville (XVIe-XIXe siècles)
candidates.quote: Bakala Etre ou enfant masculin, traduit la force, la vaillance
candidates.supports: Bakala is attested as a Beembe (Kongo group, Congo-Brazzaville) personal name with a stated meaning. It does not call Bakala a clan name, so it does not support nameSystem clan_name. Opened and read in this session.

verifications.claim: id: PAT_BALDE; nameMain: Baldé; nameSystem: clan_name; transmissionMode: patrilineal; designatedSocialUnit: clan

candidates.title: Fulas e Mandingas na luta pelo poder e conquista do Império de Kaabu (UNILAB, 2019)
candidates.quote: os do clã ururó, o nome de Baldé
candidates.supports: Baldé is the name used by one Fula clan (ururó) in Guinea-Bissau, quoting Tcherno Djaló 2013, p. 72; supports the clan-name and patrilineal parts of the claim. Quote copied from the fiche's own source note, where an earlier pass recorded it; not re-opened in this session.

candidates.title: La Guinée française : races, religions, coutumes, production, commerce (Arcin, 1907)
candidates.supports: Colonial administrator's equivalence of the Ourouro group with the names Ba or Baldé (p. 289); colonial source, cited for the forms it reports. Quote copied from the fiche's own source note, where an earlier pass recorded it; not re-opened in this session.

verifications.claim: id: PAT_BALOGUN; nameMain: Balogun; nameSystem: non_hereditary_patronymic; transmissionMode: patrilineal; designatedSocialUnit: individual

candidates.title: The History of the Yorubas (Samuel Johnson, 1921)
candidates.quote: The term Balogun is contracted from Iba-li-Ogun i.e. lord in war
candidates.supports: Balogun is first a Yoruba war-chief title (p. 133); supports the title origin, not the non_hereditary_patronymic system. Quote copied from the fiche's own source note, where an earlier pass recorded it; not re-opened in this session.

verifications.claim: id: PAT_BALOYI; nameMain: Baloyi; nameSystem: clan_name; transmissionMode: other; designatedSocialUnit: clan

candidates.title: The Life of a South African Tribe, vol. I : The Social Life (Junod, 1912)
candidates.quote: first the Baloyi or Ba-ka-Baloyi, in the triangle formed by the two rivers northward of their confluence
candidates.supports: Baloyi (Ba-ka-Baloyi) is a Thonga/Tsonga group in the Limpopo-Olifants area (p. 17); supports the clan-name and Tsonga association. Colonial missionary source. Quote copied from the fiche's own source note, where an earlier pass recorded it; not re-opened in this session.
